title: Agent Lifecycle History Response
description: Lane 3 (2026-09-27): GET .../agent-readiness/{agent_id}/lifecycle-history. Closed, content-free, paginated view of the agent-lifecycle-record revisions bridged onto one fleet Agent. The single-record READ route (GET .../agent-lifecycle/agent-revisions/{agent_revision_ref}/record, agent_lifecycle_record/agent_lifecycle_record_response_schema.json) already exists, but agent_lifecycle_records are grouped by an independent agent_ref with no foreign key to fleet Agent.id -- this response is the bridge, not a duplicate of that record. Each item names one (agent_revision_ref, record_ref) pair the backend included because the record's own experiment_run_id, or any of that revision's run plans' experiment_run_id, resolves to an ExperimentRun whose Experiment.agent_id equals the requested fleet agent_id (EXISTS predicates only; a revision is never expanded or matched via its agent_ref). association_basis is therefore always the single closed value EXPERIMENT_RUN_LINK: this association is DERIVED from an experiment-run link, is NOT a causal or produced/improved-by claim, and the linked revision's own history may include runs outside this agent. This response carries no attribution, no actor/user identity, and no record content -- only opaque lifecycle handles, a backend-issued timestamp, and the closed association vocabulary. Ordering (record created_at ASC, record id ASC, revision id ASC) and owner-scope/tenant/project filtering happen before pagination and before total is computed, so a visible agent with nothing visible returns 200 with items:[] and pagination.total:0 -- not distinguishable at the schema level from an agent with genuinely no linked history. x-asserted-against-backend is set false on the owning path operation: no SDK calls agent-lifecycle Routes 1-4 yet, so production volume through this bridge is expected to be ~0 at launch.

schema_version.description: Closed public wire-version discriminator; never a product/version claim.

items.description: One entry per bridged (agent_revision_ref, record_ref) pair, ordered record created_at ASC, record id ASC, revision id ASC. Never a superset of one page (bounded by pagination.per_page, itself bounded 1..50).
One bridged revision/record pair. Content-free: an opaque revision handle, an opaque record handle, the record's own creation timestamp, and the closed reason the pair is included -- nothing else.

agent_revision_ref.description: The exact immutable agent revision this history entry is about. Never the fleet Agent.id itself and never the lifecycle-record's own agent_ref -- this route bridges through experiment-run links only.

record_ref.description: The lifecycle record naming agent_revision_ref. Resolvable via GET .../agent-lifecycle/agent-revisions/{agent_revision_ref}/record for the full record projection; never minted or mutated by this read route.

created_at.description: The lifecycle record's own initial Backend issuance time; immutable. Not this bridge's own computation time and not an experiment-run timestamp.

association_basis.description: Closed single-member vocabulary: the pair is included solely because an experiment-run link resolved to this fleet agent (record.experiment_run_id or one of the revision's run plans' experiment_run_id -> ExperimentRun.Experiment.agent_id). A derived association, never a causal ('caused'/'produced'/'improved') claim, and never an attribution of authorship or actor identity.

pagination.description: Closed pagination block computed AFTER tenant/project/owner-scope filtering and association resolution -- hidden rows contribute to neither items nor total.

page.description: The requested (or default) 1-indexed page number, echoed back.

per_page.description: The requested (or default) page size, echoed back; bounded 1..50.

total.description: Total visible bridged pairs across all pages, computed after owner-scope/tenant/project filtering.
